The GNP and ZnO were mechanically homogenized using planetary ball milling (PBM) at a ratio of 1:1.
FE-SEM images showed that the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites formed a disordered crystallite layered-structure material.
The GNP/ZnO nanocomposites achieved the lowest reflection loss (RL) value of -28.21 dB at 8.45 GHz.
The through power of the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites was calculated to be 99.84%.
The crystallite size of ZnO was 63.4 nm with a crystallinity percentage of 82.95%.
The crystallite size of the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites was 19.3 nm with a crystallinity percentage of 81.8%.
The FE-SEM, XRD, and FTIR results confirmed the successful formation of the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites.

The disordered crystallite layered-structure, smaller particle size, and presence of specific functional groups in the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites contributed to their excellent microwave absorption performance.
The GNP/ZnO nanocomposites showed promising potential as a lightweight and advanced functional material for future stealth aircraft applications in the military sector.
The microwave absorption performance of the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites was superior to the individual GNP and ZnO precursors.
The mechanical homogenization using planetary ball milling (PBM) was a green and cost-effective method for synthesizing the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites.
The layered carbon sheets in the GNP and the alteration in the crystallite structure of ZnO were observed using FE-SEM and XRD, respectively.
The FTIR spectroscopy confirmed the presence of specific functional groups in the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites.
The GNP/ZnO nanocomposites exhibited strong microwave polarization capabilities, leading to their excellent microwave absorption properties.
The disordered crystallite layered-structure of the GNP/ZnO nanocomposites allowed for efficient dielectric loss and interface/dipole polarization, enhancing their microwave absorption performance.
